title: UiNode
description: The declared UI schema (platform plan 6.2): a page is a tree of these nodes, rendered natively by React (web shell, PWA) today and by SwiftUI (iPhone, Apple TV) later. Session B step 5 adds List, CardGrid, MediaShelf, DetailPane and SplitView (platform plan 6.2's named generic primitives) alongside v0's Chat-only set; see docs/dev.md's 'A2UI' entry for exactly which pages this session converted to real schema pages and which stayed hand-written React, and why.

source.description: route: the app's own backend route. host: a host.* RPC method (4.9). package: a data call of the package whose page this is (APP-KIND-01); `path` is then a `contributes.data[]` id, never a URL, and the call is POST /api/plugins/<package id>/data/<path>.

stream.description: True when this binding delivers incremental updates (turn.token during a Chat reply, 7.2) rather than one value.

params.description: Source "package" only: the JSON body of the data call. Each value is a literal or the string "$state.<name>", read from page state at call time (a picker writes it). A value that is an object with numeric `lat` and `lon` (Current location) travels in the body only and is never part of a query key, URL, log or cache.

package_binding.description: A binding whose source is "package": the nodes that draw a package's own data (answer_blocks, picker) take only this.

state.description: NEWS-00: a literal map written into the target page's state on arrival (a channel page reads its `kind` and `key` this way). String values may contain `{field}` placeholders, resolved from the bound list item or card the action fires for (as `call.args` do); a value is never read from another page's state.

target.description: A route or host.* method. May contain a `{field}` placeholder (a bound list item's own field, substituted per item/per selected item by a list's row_action or batch action).

args.description: String values may contain `{field}` placeholders, resolved the same way as `target`.

play.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: hand a media item to the host's player (the shell's audio session). `media_id` may contain `{field}` placeholders, resolved from the bound item the action fires for (`{id}`). The page never plays anything itself; a host with no player refuses the action with a message.

position_s.description: The start position in seconds. String values may contain `{field}` placeholders resolved from the bound item.

prompt.description: May contain `{field}`/`{count}` placeholders, resolved against the same item(s) `on_confirm` will act on.

action.description: Exactly one of the five declared actions (6.2).

tone.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: the page tone. cinema: the dark media tone (the kit's `cinema` token set, the same in light and dark themes) over the whole screen while this page shows; the media apps select it. A client without the tone draws the default.

condition.description: A simple expression string evaluated against page state; absent means always shown.

message_thread.description: The Chat pattern component (6.2 names Chat as one of the three hardest pages to express; this is the pattern component that resulted, not one of the plan's named generic primitives). Session B step 4 rebuilt Chat on @assistant-ui/react, which owns its own history loading, streaming, thread list and message actions entirely inside React (chatModelAdapter.ts, chatThreadListAdapter.ts) - v0's bind/sender_field/text_field described a generic turn-list interpreter never built (see git history on this file); this node is now just a mount point, the same role `settings_editor` plays for Settings.

settings_editor.description: Mounts the kit's own settings renderer (frontend/src/kit/settings/SettingsRenderer.tsx), which already reads the settings registry generically (docs/SETTINGS.md's 'one definition, the generic renderer') - a second, JSON-authored description of the same data would be a competing source of truth, not a schema page in the sense the other nodes here are. Session B step 7 ('settings as an editor') extends that renderer directly (a tree sidebar, search, scope tabs); this node's own shape never changes.

scope.description: selected: the interpreter loops `action` once per currently-selected item, substituting `{field}` placeholders from that item. all: loops over every currently-loaded item regardless of selection (docs/BACKLOG.md's 'clear-all where the whole list is disposable').

list.description: The kit's List primitive (frontend/src/kit/primitives/List.tsx), bound to one route that returns an array. Content-agnostic like the primitive it wraps: a row shows item_label_field as its title and, when given, item_subtitle_field/item_badge_field underneath - a single-line-per-field template, not a full custom renderItem (a page needing richer per-row layout than that stays hand-written React; docs/plans/session-b-ui.md step 5's recorded decision on People and Privacy).

item_subtitle_field.description: A `{field}` template string (the same substitution as action.call's target/args), not a bare dotted path - lets a row's subtitle combine more than one field ('{category} · {scope}') without a richer per-row template mechanism.

item_badge_field.description: Dotted path to a boolean; true shows a small badge (item_badge_label) next to the subtitle.

item_media_field.description: NEWS-00: dotted path to a lucide icon name or a same-origin image path (starting with `/`); drawn as the row's leading media. An address with a scheme or host is refused, so a row never loads another site's picture.

row_toggle.description: NEWS-00: a per-row switch (Follow, Save). `field` is the dotted path to a boolean on the row; the action is fired with the row's fields and `on` set to the new value.

card_grid.description: The kit's CardGrid primitive (frontend/src/kit/primitives/CardGrid.tsx). No page uses this yet (platform plan 6.2: Videos/Music, not in this session's scope) - added now for catalog/schema completeness (docs/plans/session-b-ui.md step 5's own agreement test), same minimal single-field-per-card shape as `list`.

media_shelf.description: The kit's MediaShelf primitive (ui/src/primitives/MediaShelf.tsx): a sideways rail of media tiles at one declared aspect (wide 16:9, poster 2:3, square 1:1). MEDIA-PLAYER-01 adds the heading, a caption subtitle, the played-share bar, a corner badge and a running-time label; on a package page `on_select` may be a `play` action.

heading.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: the shelf's heading ("Continue watching"), which also names the rail.

item_subtitle_field.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: a `{field}` template for the caption's second line (the channel, the artist), as list.item_subtitle_field.

item_media_field.description: Dotted path to the tile's same-origin image path (starting with `/`). An address with a scheme or a host is not loaded.

item_progress_field.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: dotted path to the played share, a number 0 to 1, drawn as a bar along the tile's bottom edge.

item_badge_field.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: dotted path to a short string drawn as the tile's corner badge ("Saved", "On this phone", "Not saved"); empty draws none.

item_meta_field.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: dotted path to the running time, a number of seconds (drawn as 18:42) or a short string.

variant.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: card draws the shelf inside a bordered section card; plain draws a frameless row (a heading, the optional See all link, then the tiles), as the media apps and News do.

orientation.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: horizontal is the sideways rail; vertical stacks the tiles as rows, the picture at the start and the caption beside it (Up next beside a player).

layout.description: Grid wraps whole tiles from the existing card-size budget, with two columns on a phone. Vertical orientation takes precedence.

art_shape.description: Circle uses square artwork clipped to a circle, including its current ring.

density.description: Compact vertical rows have 72 px artwork, two caption lines and trailing item_meta_field running time. Horizontal shelves use the existing card-size budget.

item_highlight_field.description: Dotted path to a boolean; true marks the current track or next episode with the media current ring token and aria-current.

item_index_field.description: Dotted path to the leading track index in a vertical row; zero is displayed.

row_actions.description: Vertical row controls outside the artwork button. Play is icon-only; other actions are labelled pills. Labels may contain {field} placeholders; a nonempty label_field value overrides the label. Each action receives its row, just like on_select.

hide_when_empty.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: draw nothing (no heading, no empty state) when the bound call returns no rows, so a shelf with nothing in it is simply absent. A load error still shows.

see_all.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: a link beside the heading ("See all"), usually a `navigate` to the app's full list. Fired with no row.

billboard.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: the kit's Billboard block (ui/src/primitives/Billboard.tsx), a rotating hero of bound rows composed from the kit carousel: backdrop art, an eyebrow line, the title, a subtitle, a primary action (Play) and up to two secondary ones. Autoplay pauses on hover, on focus, on a hidden tab and under reduced motion.

size.description: card: a rounded card in the page flow. hero: full width and taller, the title set large (Shows and Films). banner (MEDIA-POLISH-01): a short 340 px band from 640 px, so the first shelf shows under it (Videos); on a phone it grows with its words.

item_eyebrow_field.description: A `{field}` template for the small line over the title.

item_art_field.description: Dotted path to the backdrop's same-origin image path.

hide_when_empty.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: draw nothing when the bound call returns no rows (as media_shelf.hide_when_empty).

billboard_action.description: One Billboard button: its words, an optional lucide icon name, and the action it fires with the slide's row.

player.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: the kit's Player (ui/src/primitives/Player.tsx) for one bound media item. The bound call returns the item (an object, or rows whose first row is used). Default field names: id, src, title, subtitle, poster, chapters [{start_s, title}], captions [{src, srclang, label, kind?, default?}], thumbnails (a storyboard WebVTT path), position_s, completed, up_next {id, title, subtitle?, art?}.

layout.description: Default: video for kind video, audio for kind audio.

autoplay_next.description: Count down and play up_next when the item ends. Off by default; a child's page leaves it off.

fields.description: Dotted paths that override the default field names.

on_progress.description: Fired every 10 s while playing, on pause, on seek, at the end and on unload. Placeholders: the item's own fields plus {position_s}, {duration_s}, {reason} and {completed}.

on_next.description: Fired with the up_next item's fields (a `play`, or a `navigate` to its watch page).

details.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: draw the item's title and subtitle line under the picture (a watch page's title block).

actions.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: the actions row under the title (Like, Watch later, Share to a screen). Each button fires its action with the item's fields. With `field`, the button is a toggle: pressed while that boolean field of the item is true, labelled `on_label` then, and fired with `on` set to the new value; the item is read again afterwards.

field.description: Dotted path to a boolean on the item.

reader.description: MEDIA-BOOKS-01: one bound book (an object or the first row), drawn by the kit Reader. Default fields: id, src (same-origin URL), title, format (epub or pdf), locator ({kind: cfi, cfi, spine_index?, block_index?} or {kind: page, page}, 1-based). Heavy engines load only when a book opens.

format.description: Override the bound format field; absent reads fields.format or format.

font_size.description: EPUB font step: 85, 100, 115, 130, 150, 175 or 200 percent. PDF ignores it.

fields.description: Dotted field paths overriding the default book fields; locator is the saved reader locator, for example position.locator.

on_locator.description: Debounced 250 ms after relocation, flushed on close, hide and unmount. Receives the item's fields plus {locator} (a JSON object) and {percent} (number, 0 to 100); nested placeholders such as {locator.cfi} work too. Quiet calls do not refetch the binding.

on_close.description: Draw Close and fire with the book's fields after flushing pending progress.

detail_pane.description: The kit's DetailPane primitive (frontend/src/kit/primitives/DetailPane.tsx): the 'one thing, in full' half of a SplitView. Not used by any page this session builds; added for catalog/schema completeness.

split_view.description: The kit's SplitView primitive (ui/src/primitives/SplitView.tsx). Two forms: `list` and `detail` (an index beside one item, taking turns on a phone), or MEDIA-POLISH-01's `main` and `aside` (a wide column with a narrow one beside it from 1024 px, stacked below that: a player with Up next). A package page may use the main and aside form.

aside_label.description: The aside column's accessible name ("Up next").

widget_card.description: Renders the actor's `size: "card"` widgets (D to E's `contributes.widgets[]` contract, docs/plans/wave-2.md) in a grid sized by the kit's card-size slider (frontend/src/kit/primitives/CardSizeSlider.tsx, 180-560px, per app per device). Not a `card_grid` bound straight to display rows: `bind` resolves to the widget list only (`GET /api/widgets`); each widget's own display data (`GET /api/widgets/:package/:id/data`) is a second, per-widget fetch the interpreter makes on that widget's own `refresh_s`, since the list route and the data route are two different calls by design (the list is cheap and shared, the data is per-package and cached server-side).

widget_row.description: The `size: "row"` counterpart to `widget_card`: same binding and per-widget data fetch, a slim horizontal row instead of a sized grid tile - no card-size slider applies (a row's height is fixed; only a grid of cards has a size to pick).

answer_blocks.description: Draws the answer blocks a package data call returns (APP-KIND-02), each through the kit's one answer-block dispatcher (validation, then the kit Element named by `kind`; an unknown kind or invalid props shows the block's `alt` sentence). A page's hero is a first node of this type. `bind` is a package binding whose data call returns {blocks}.

kinds.description: Draw only blocks of these kinds, so a page can place one kind per section. Absent: every block returned.

filter_state.description: NEWS-LOOK-02: the page-state key the block's filter chips write when one is chosen (the chip's `id`; an empty id means All). The page's data call reads it back through `$state.<key>` in its bind params. Without it the chips are not drawn.

states.description: WEATHER-FIX-01: what the page says when its data call cannot draw blocks for a stated reason, in the page's own words. `needs_place`: the call answered {needs: "place"} (the person has no place chosen) or failed with code needs_place. `down`: the source could not be reached (code down). `timed_out`: it took too long (code timed_out). Any other empty or failed call keeps `empty_state` and the generic retry.

actions.description: NEWS-00: the actions a block may fire, by role. A block fires an entry with the item's own ids and never names a route itself. `open` navigates to a story and `open_channel` to a channel (the ids are `channel_kind` and `channel_key`), `save`, `follow`, `feedback` and `summarize` call, `reset_mix` asks first (`confirm`), `listen` plays. A package page's entries stay under its own `/api/plugins/<id>/` and `/apps/<id>/` prefixes (spec/ui/app-check.ts).

data_state.description: A stated reason for an answer_blocks node with nothing to draw: an icon, an optional title, the sentence, and up to three buttons.

to.description: A screen of this app: /apps/<id>..., or its own settings area /settings/<id>.

state.description: The page-state name set to "current" with the device coordinates in `<state>_geo`, on this click only.

tabs.description: NEWS-00: peer views of one page (Topics and Sources, say), drawn by the kit's Tabs primitive. Peer views only: the shell owns navigation between pages (UI.md). The active tab is page state `state` (default: the first tab), mirrored in the URL by the shell.

picker.description: Chooses one value and writes it to page state (APP-KIND-02), drawn with the kit's select primitive. Fixed `leading` options come first, then the rows of `bind` (a package data call returning {rows}). A section's `condition` reads the state it writes.

variant.description: Pill reuses TabsList variant pill for leading options and bound rows (for example seasons), reading selection from page state and writing the chosen row key.

state.description: The page-state name this picker writes.

label.description: The accessible name of the control.

placeholder.description: Shown while nothing is chosen (for example "Default place").

needs.description: Choosing this option asks the browser for the device location, on that choice only. The coordinates stay in memory as page state `<state>_geo` ({lat, lon}); they are never stored.

search.description: NEWS-LOOK-02: a search field that writes what is typed to page state (debounced) and, on Enter, fires `submit` with the item {q}, so `{q}` placeholders in a navigate state or call args fill from it. With `recents` bound and the field empty it draws the rows as chips (a chip sets the state key to its label and fires `submit`); `clear_recents` fires from a Clear button. The node sends nothing itself.

state.description: The page-state key the typed text is written to.

item_key_field.description: The recents row's key field. Default `key`.

item_label_field.description: The recents row's label field. Default `label`.

nav_entry.description: One row in the shell's nav (docs/plans/session-b-ui.md step 2, frontend/src/shell/nav.ts). Not part of the root `oneOf` above: a nav entry is never a page-body node a page's `body`/`children` array renders - it describes the shell's own chrome, the same distinction `page` (a route) already draws from `section`/`form` (page content). A package's manifest `contributes.pages[]` entry emits this shape minus `to` (design-resolver, 2026-09-06, docs/BACKLOG.md's `app`-kind item): `icon` and `label` carry over as-is, and the shell derives `to` from the package and page ids (`/apps/<package id>/<page id>`) rather than trusting a package to name its own route. Core's own pages still declare this shape by hand in nav.ts today.

to.description: A route path, matching a `page.id`'s route.
